text:
maya: FYI we had a POST with ~1k mixed-dim embeds (256/512/768/1024) gzipped in one request. ingress was stuck for ~45s and p99 hopped.
oliver: ouch. splitter returned some 413s but most of the time continuous-batching held the connection open and ate slots.
tess: what if instead of telling clients to chunk, we accept a large payload via preflight-pre-sign and do server-side chunking/scheduling? client uploads the big file to S3, we queue a server-side splitter job that emits smaller embed jobs. response is 202 with job id and minimal retry churn.
maya: interesting. that avoids client churn and handles heavyweight uploads without blocking fastpath. security considerations though: we need presigned URLs scoped and short-lived and scanning for malformed payloads.
console-pm: console UX: show an "Upload large batch" flow on the Embeddings route. On paste, show estimate and a button "Upload & let Redwood split (recommended)". Show estimated units, estimated cost, and an "advanced: client-chunk locally" option.
sdk-eng: SDK support needed: helper to preflight (dims+bytes) -> get presign URL and suggested chunk_size; perform upload; then call /embeds/async with upload metadata. SDK can poll job status or watch via websocket. We'll add helper that transparently falls back to client-chunk if presign flow not allowed. Also emit header on eventual embed jobs: `X-Embed-Origin: server-split` so telemetry ties back.
telemetry-bot: telemetry plan: emit events `embeds.preflight.units_estimate`, `embeds.upload.bytes_bucket`, `embeds.server_split.count`, `embeds.async.job_latency_ms`, `embeds.server_split.success_pct`. Keep cardinality low via buckets.
oliver: flow sketch: 1) client calls POST /embeds/preflight with dims header + compressed_size -> server returns JSON {estimated_units, suggested_chunk, presign_url} (if eligible). 2) client PUT to presign_url. 3) client POST /embeds/async-start referencing upload id -> server returns 202 {job_id, status_url}. 4) server-side splitter reads upload, emits normal embed jobs to runtime, marks job done. 5) server posts webhook or client polls status_url.
tess: fallback: if presign not available or tenant opts out, return structured 4xx with `suggested_chunk` header like `X-Embed-Suggest:100` and a human-friendly body.
console-pm: on the Console, show estimated units before upload and an opt-in toggle "Enable server-side splitting" per API key. Also show progress for async jobs and a link to results (embeddings returned or stored artifacts).
sdk-eng: we'll add `auto_server_split:true` flag in SDK and handle 202 job. We'll set `X-Embed-Client-AutoSplit: true` on the preflight to signal opt-in, and `X-Embed-Client-Poll:true` when polling so telemetry knows who waited vs webhook.
maya: runtime protection: immediate preflight check at LB to avoid handing heavy payload to continuous-batcher. If presign flow is returned we accept upload; otherwise fast-reject with hint. Also ensure server-split job has backpressure so splitting doesn't saturate runtime.
telemetry-bot: schema registered: embeds.asyncsplit.v1 with fields: preflight_units_bucket, upload_bytes_bucket, server_split_chunks_bucket, job_latency_bucket, origin_header.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: embeds-async-split v0.1 -> staging (sha: f00b4r).
console-pm: rollout plan: 1) metrics-only preflight for 2w; 2) enable presign+async-split as opt-in via Console toggle for select tenants; 3) 10% rollout; 4) global. We'll add clear docs and SDK examples.
maya: tests: e2e with gzipped framed payloads, a failure mode test (malformed items), and a security scan on presign lifecycle. Also bench the server-split throughput.
tess: good. watch SLO during canary; tag @eng-oncall for the 10% flip.
sdk-eng: we'll add transparent fallback to client-chunk in SDK to avoid hard failures for older clients.
deploy-bot: deploy started: embeds-async-split v0.1 -> staging (sha: f00b4r). :rocket:
